All default, --describe, --scheduler-test, and --test-only actions are read-only.

superseded_launches.proof_scope: Launch7 started all twenty fresh generation-zero cells. Four cells completed 25k and terminal evaluation; sixteen sealed exact USR1 READY checkpoints, then failed deterministically because /usr/local/bin/scontrol was absent from every observed GPU compute-node image. No REQUEUE_CALLING or replacement generation exists and the reporter was cancelled with DependencyNeverSatisfied. The full read-only terminal census is protocol-bound by launch7_negative_provenance.json. Every Launch7 output, checkpoint, W&B identity, task state, receipt, job ID, and namespace is negative evidence only and cannot enter Launch8.

design.fresh_start_policy: Every Launch8 wave-zero cell starts from scratch in the fresh Launch8 namespace; no checkpoint, result, optimizer, model initialization, W&B identity, or state from any superseded launch may be imported, reused, resumed, retried, or recovered. Resume=auto and W&B resume are permitted only for the exact same fresh Launch8 cell in the predeclared, authorization-bound wave-zero to wave-one DAG.
design.common_random_numbers: Within each setting and seed, GS and GSEP use identical initialization seed, published-union data identity/order, validation sample seed, evaluation seed bank, and evaluation profile.
design.midpoint_policy: No selection, promotion, dropping, early-stopping, or arm-dependent decision occurs at 5k or 12.5k; all cells continue to 25k.

causal_contrast.zero_weight_control_policy: In the outcome-blind controlled CPU reconstruction, GS materializes identical executable-prefix targets, action projection, losses, artifacts, and telemetry but contributes exactly zero effective objective weight.
required_parity: independently composed launch contract after deleting only run/W&B identity and the three weight-caused hashes/leaves
independently loaded data and sampler identity
controlled CPU scratch parameter bytes and RNG state before the audited forward
raw target/artifact hashes and telemetry values
causal_contrast.parity_failure_policy: Reject the entire pilot before training.

core_binding.action_bounds_contract: Per-setting loss and planner bounds are derived from, equal to, and hash-bound to the actual environment Box in weight_audit.lock.json; absence or disagreement fails closed.

scientific_contract.prefix_length_rule: For every matched branch independently, p=min(4, logged selected continuation horizon); learned horizon is never used.

acceptance.scope: GSEP must pass every absolute gate in all ten cells at both 5k and 25k. GS must pass structural, finite, target-completeness, target-parity, and zero-weight gates; its gauge, clipping saturation, calibration, method, and outcome values remain causal observations.

prefix_structural_gates.target_rule: Before launch, independently source-derive and freeze the full branchwise length-vector/distribution and hmax64 mask contract. Actual runs bind the exact fixed-validation sampler summary and aggregate scalar denominators; prefix_steps_mean is descriptive and is never compared to 4.

report_contract.input: one immutable JSON report bundle assembled only after all 20 terminal triplets verify; its root binds the live-verified package protocol, canonical manifest, trainer fingerprint, and all four outcome-blind audit artifacts; gate.py itself never reads live run directories
report_contract.outcome_blind_until: All training, telemetry, and calibration gates are computed before final outcomes are opened.
report_contract.decision: accept only if structural, candidate absolute, paired calibration, candidate absolute outcome, and paired outcome gates all pass; otherwise reject

launch_contract.terminal_final_evaluation_episode_policy: Exactly task IDs 1..5 x episode indices 0..4 using the bounded-objective legacy fallback seed eval.seed + 1000*task_index + episode_index; the protocol table published by the trainer is provenance only and is not the consumed seed schedule.
launch_contract.resume_policy: Only wave one may resume, and only from the same Launch8 cell's exact wave-zero CONTINUATION_READY checkpoint after verifying the durable graph authorization and predecessor array identity; no foreign or superseded state is accepted.
launch_contract.trainer_invocation_policy: Each cell uses one uninterrupted scratch-to-25k scientific identity with resume=auto and no TREEWM_STOP_AFTER_UPDATE in any process or environment. Update 5k is retrospective telemetry analysis only, never a lifecycle stage.
launch_contract.dependency: held wave-zero 20-cell GPU array; wave-one 20-cell GPU array with afterok and kill-on-invalid-dep on wave zero; one CPU report-and-gate job with afterok and kill-on-invalid-dep on wave one; release wave zero only after durable graph authorization and receipt

runtime_feasibility.evidence_source: launch7_negative_provenance.json plus its hash-bound completed-cell logs and scheduler rows
runtime_feasibility.conclusion: The slowest Launch7 READY checkpoint leaves at most 7482 updates. Reserving 180 seconds for terminal evaluation, W&B finalization, and worker completion still requires less than 44% of the conservative Launch7 minimum pre-signal update rate. This is feasibility evidence, not permission to consume Launch7 state.

real_gpu_two_wave_canary.runtime_proof_scope: The canary proves isolated lexical pinned-Python execution, Torch import from one of the two validated nonsymlink package-root directories, exactly one visible selected CUDA device, a real CUDA tensor operation, and checkpoint transfer across the two waves. It does not hash or version-bind the resolved interpreter binary, pyvenv.cfg, Torch distribution/native libraries, CUDA driver/runtime, or establish byte-equivalence to the scientific trainer environment.

production_authorization_evidence.post_acceptance_change_scope: Post-acceptance package changes are limited to canary historical-identity, canonical-path, lock/rollback, and cleanup-only recovery guards in two_wave_canary.py, plus mandatory accepted-canary prerequisite and report-versus-cancel gating with cleanup-only legacy recovery in submit.py and report.py and matching prerequisite validation in worker.py and train_entry.py, plus a one-generation append-only terminal-report repair controller and a repair-only publication mode in report.py after the original Launch8 reporter failed during immutable publication; fresh canary DAG submission commands, scalar dependency forms, wave0 release payload, canary compute worker and Slurm scripts, and fresh scientific DAG submission commands and dependency forms remain unchanged

launch_contract.source_snapshot: immutable, read-only, nonsymlinked, byte-verified source/config/package snapshot bound to commit, runtime, protocol, manifest, audit, and resolved launch identities

execution.training_lifecycle: wave zero creates the fresh scratch-to-25000 identity; on USR1 it seals CONTINUATION_READY and exits scheduler-success without requeue; predeclared afterok wave one either resumes that exact checkpoint, authenticates wave-zero completion and no-ops, or fails nonzero if another USR1 arrives before completion
execution.process_topology: submission-host controller submits held wave0 array -> afterok wave1 array -> afterok report; each GPU task is Slurm batch shell -> worker.py -> train_entry.py -> in-process scripts.train; no srun, compute-side scheduler client, or within-wave requeue
execution.scheduler_client_placement: Only submit.py, cancel.py, report_repair.py, and submission-host recovery may execute scontrol/squeue/sbatch/scancel. Compute worker.py, train.slurm, report.py, and report_repair.slurm never do.

scheduler_control_plane.trust_model: root-admin mutable scheduler control plane; config and Lua policy bytes are observation-bound from preclaim through submission; root-owned Slurm clients, plugin binaries, and shared libraries are trusted mutable external runtime
